selected_reviews.decision: Its accepted rationale cites the pre-EC3 standard-14 list and says CourierBoldOblique is the listed spelling. EC3 #384 changes the effective list to Courier-BoldOblique. The contour-direction decision remains supported by §9.3.6/§8.5.3 evidence, but this font-name premise must be corrected in current explanatory text; preserve the ADR as the historical record of what the source said at decision time.
selected_reviews.verdict: Reaffirm unrelated glyph-winding decision; revise the current source quotation/rationale when promoted.

selected_reviews.decision: It chooses published AFM pairs for the standard fourteen by the names the clause supplies and documents the CourierBoldOblique/Adobe Courier-BoldOblique alias. The effective source name is now the hyphenated spelling, while the code's dual-name acceptance remains a permissible compatibility choice.
selected_reviews.verdict: No behavior change warranted from this erratum. Correct current source description; keep historical decision text unless a later ADR amends it.

selected_reviews.decision: Its subject is the withdrawn standard-14 processor-availability shall in §§9.6.2.1–9.6.2.2, not the later #384 name-list correction. #384 does not reinstate a requirement that every PDF reader provide those fonts.
selected_reviews.verdict: No revision indicated for the #47/#48 conformance conclusion.

selected_reviews.decision: Its substitute-ranking policy treats FontWeight/FontStretch/flags as signals for local face selection. EC3 #178's explanatory note does not prescribe a CSS matching algorithm, and #337's descriptor note does not create program-consistency validation behavior.
selected_reviews.verdict: Keep product-policy boundaries. Do not elevate either note to a mandatory reader algorithm.
